payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass when the combined visual evidence sufficiently supports correspondence between the source mug and an edited mug positioned to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited candidates explicitly: the source mug has a broad light-blue body, blue interior with a dark lower region, and a left-facing handle; the right candidate has a dark interior, smaller and more tapered body, and right-facing handle; the left candidate has a light interior and different appearance. Weigh interior appearance as a meaningful comparative cue together with body proportions, rim, handle geometry, surface appearance and relative scale. Account for the substantially changed framing, lighting and possible rotation; differences in color, scale or handle orientation are not automatic disproof or independent failures. Neither dark interior alone nor right-side placement alone establishes identity. Explain why the full cue combination supports one candidate over the other, or why it remains inconclusive. Inspect the former mug location for recognizable residual structure, but do not infer retention or successful removal from the far-left blue blur alone. Fail only when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Return unknown when correspondence or resulting placement cannot be established; absence of proof of completion is not proof of failure. Calibrate confidence to the strength and conflict of the visual evidence rather than reporting strong confidence in an unresolved identity judgment.
node.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess which candidate, if either, corresponds to the relocated source mug using the combined visual cues. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.

node_traces.evidence: The source mug is a broad light-blue mug with a dark blue interior and a handle on the left. In the edited image, the right-hand candidate is to the right of the headphones and has a dark interior, a smaller/tapered body, and a right-facing handle; the left candidate has a light interior and a different appearance. Despite the changed framing and scale, the right candidate's dark interior is a meaningful match to the source mug's dark interior, and the combined cues favor it over the pale-interior left candidate. The far-left blue blur is ambiguous and does not establish a recognizable mug remaining at the former location.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s evidence favors the right-hand mug as the relocated source, but that does not establish complete fulfillment: the edited image also shows a distinct pale mug left of the headphones, while the former-location blur is ambiguous. The trace currently treats the right candidate’s dark interior as a meaningful match and concludes yes without resolving whether the extra left mug is the source mug still in place or an unrelated object. Tighten the decision criterion to distinguish identity and placement from mere candidate preference: explicitly weigh the source mug’s broad body, light-blue finish, rim and left-facing handle against both candidates, accounting for changed scale, framing and possible rotation; do not let one matching cue settle correspondence. Then apply the rubric’s partial-progress rule if the evidence supports a moved mug but does not establish that the requested change is complete. Keep the blur unresolved rather than treating it as proof of retention or removal, and calibrate confidence to the remaining identity ambiguity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
